$comment: flux-expr/3 vectors (EXPR-SPEC-3 §2 to §7): a date part, date arithmetic and string concatenation, in the shape of expr2-vectors.json (EXPR-SPEC-2 §11). Every vector is read for the file's 'language' unless it names its own, which is how the refusals under flux-expr/2 sit here; a vector with side 'core' is a contract's text. Every accepted vector also runs as a DuckDB query in the test suite and must agree: EXTRACT as extract(day FROM d), ADD_DAYS as d + n, ADD_MONTHS as CAST(d + to_months(n) AS DATE), ADD_YEARS as CAST(d + to_years(n) AS DATE), and || with CAST(x AS VARCHAR) for an integer. The model is a date dimension in dsdgen's shape (date_dim, whose key is the Julian day) and an expose of edge cases (quirks: columns named year, month and day, NULLs, dates at both ends of the calendar, an enum column). No JSON number appears: a number is a decimal string; a date is YYYY-MM-DD.

vectors.expr: CASE WHEN flag THEN label || 'Q' END
